lead.hed: USS McFaul is home in Norfolk after an 11-month deployment
lead.insight: Naval Surface Force Atlantic said Friday that the Arleigh Burke-class destroyer USS McFaul returned to Naval Station Norfolk, ending an 11-month deployment to the U.S. 5th and 6th Fleet. The ship left Norfolk on Nov. 25, 2025. During the deployment it used the Aegis Combat System for anti-air warfare, surface warfare, and naval surface fire support, and operated with the Abraham Lincoln, George H.W. Bush, and George Washington carrier strike groups during Operation Epic Fury. Commanding officer Cmdr. Adam Samson said the crew protected the strike group under pressure. The ship is named for Engineman Chief Donald L. McFaul, a SEAL killed in Operation Just Cause in 1989. The official still, taken and posted today, shows sailors manning the rails at the homecoming.
lead.image_credit: Petty Officer 2nd Class Pierce Luck · DVIDS 10043770 · Public domain · Sailors man the rails aboard USS McFaul at the homecoming, Naval Station Norfolk, Oct. 23, 2026.

political.hed: Public Discourse says a 1978 citizenship history still bears on birthright citizenship
political.insight: Friday's Public Discourse bookshelf essay says James H. Kettner's 1978 book on American citizenship still matters in the fight over who is a citizen at birth. The writer ties the book to President Trump's January 2025 order on children born here to parents here unlawfully or temporarily, and to the Supreme Court litigation that followed. It is argument about the books. It does not reprint a new floor vote.

political.hed: Law & Liberty reviews a Lois Lowry novel about a world that has lost its stories
political.insight: Friday's Law & Liberty review takes up Lois Lowry's Building 903, a children's novel set in a post-literate world, and asks what a culture loses when the stories go. Lowry is 89. The piece is literary argument, not a statute.

political.hed: Heritage says the American Jewish story tests the Founders' design
political.insight: Thursday's Heritage report says the American Jewish experience is a historical test of the Founders' design, and that the point is sharper as the country marks 250 years amid renewed antisemitism and civic fracture. The piece is argument and history. It does not cite a floor vote.

tech.hed: The Army activated a Guam air-defense battalion to replace Task Force Talon
tech.insight: The Army said soldiers of 3rd Battalion, 43rd Air Defense Artillery, took part in an activation ceremony Oct. 16 at Andersen Air Force Base, Guam. The battalion will support the defense of Guam with air and missile defense. Task Force Talon had held that watch since 2013 and deactivated in July. Lt. Col. Joshua Urness, the battalion commander, said the unit now stands up the Army's contribution to the Guam Defense System. USNI News reported Friday that the battalion is meant to meet air and missile threats from China and North Korea. The fold item points at the Army release.

tech.hed: Washington says a Russian satellite shadowed a U.S.-registered radar satellite
tech.insight: Defense News reported Friday that Undersecretary of State Thomas G. DiNanno told the United Nations on Wednesday that Russia's Cosmos 2612 maneuvered dangerously close to ICEYE-X36, a U.S.-registered radar satellite whose operator supplies imagery to Ukraine. The Russian satellite spent more than two weeks closing in, then shadowed the American craft from as close as a third of a mile through the weekend of Oct. 17. DiNanno called the behavior consistent with on-orbit weapons operations. Space historian Jonathan McDowell said he believes it is the first unapproved rendezvous of two active satellites in low Earth orbit.

tech.hed: Keen Sword is still running, with Theodore Roosevelt in the Philippine Sea
tech.insight: U.S. Forces Japan said Keen Sword 27 opened Oct. 19 and runs through Oct. 29, with about 45,000 Japan Self-Defense Force personnel, 11,000 U.S. troops, 260 aircraft, and 40 ships, including the Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group. USNI News said Friday the strike group was still in the Philippine Sea as of Wednesday. The fold item points at the official exercise release.

culture.hed: Providence sets Pope Leo's Paris Mass against a weekend of French riots
culture.insight: Friday's Providence essay sets Pope Leo's first papal visit to France, and an outdoor Mass the writer says drew 800,000 people to the Champs-Élysées and Place de la Concorde, against a weekend of riots the writer says burned public buildings and looted shops. The piece reads both events as spiritual conflict. It does not reprint a police tally.
